messages:
sam: Heads up — after yesterday's analytics schema cutover were seeing ~12% lower counts on the per-route 'active_tokens' metric in the console for a subset of tenants. Not a huge outage but parity is off. :eyes:
mira: Which cohort? random sample or specific route tags?
sam: It looks concentrated on routes that hit the new 'route_profile' denorm path. Non-denorm routes look fine.
alex: Can you paste a quick diff between the old vs new query results?
sam: Sure — small example below for route_id=rt_42
```
-- old:
select sum(tokens) from route_metrics where route_id='rt_42' and ts >= '2026-03-18';
-- new:
select sum(active_tokens) from route_profile_metrics where route_id='rt_42' and ts >= '2026-03-18';
```
jordan: Might be a contract mismatch: I remember we changed null semantics — old pipeline filtered nulls earlier in aggregation, new one leaves them then uses COALESCE in the UI layer. If the UI expects no-nulls that explains -12%.
mira: I saw a few telemetry events where tokens=null after the SDK update. We didn't account for that in the mapping.
pat: Options: 1) quick rollback of the write path (painful), 2) emit a read-adapter in the console service to normalize, 3) backfill to fix missing values.
alex: Rollback is costly. We planned this for months. If it's just nulls, a read-adapter or UI normalization should be fastest and lowest risk for customers.
sam: Agree — but watch out: some downstream billing ETL uses the old table directly (billing team flagged earlier). We need to ensure parity for billing or we'll invoice incorrectly.
mira: Can we gate fix with a feature flag and enable in canary tenants first?
jordan: Yes — we can ship a small adapter that does COALESCE(active_tokens, 0) and also maps weird route tags back to canonical keys. Rollout via ff-service to 5% -> 25% -> all.
pat: Backfill is still on the table if numbers don't reconcile in 48h. We should capture a diff snapshot now for the audit.
sam: I'll dump a snapshot and post link in #eng-platform after a quick scrub.

deploy-bot: scheduled rollout: console-read-adapter v0.1 -> canary group (5%) at 2026-03-21T02:00Z. triggered by sam

alex: One more twist — the new denorm introduced route_profile_id which aliases old route_id in some ephemeral cases (multi-route fusion). The mapping logic currently prefers route_profile_id and can drop legacy route tags if not present. That can cause counts to be attributed to a merged profile instead of original route.
mira: Hmm. That explains odd spikes where one profile shows +20% and another shows -12%.
jordan: Proposed action plan:
- ship read-adapter with normalization + COALESCE (canary) [owner: jordan]
- snapshot diffs for last 7 days and send to billing for review [owner: sam]
- instrument metrics comparison job that runs hourly to measure parity and auto-alert at >2% drift [owner: alex]
- if drift persists after 48h, schedule backfill window and post rollback checklist [owner: pat]

sam: I'll also add a small eval harness that replays a subset of ingest events through both write paths to detect semantic differences.

pat: For the backfill: reminder that indexes on the large metrics table cause IO spikes. If we go that route, we should do a throttled, shard-scoped backfill and prefer online COPY updates.
alex: And add a safety flag to prevent backfill touching tenants with active dedup windows. We learned that the hard way last year.
mira: Can we quickly add a telemetry tag on the migrated events: migration_v=1 so we can easily filter when running the parity job?
jordan: Done — read-adapter will also stamp migration_v=1 on normalized reads until the flag flips.
sam: timeline sounds good. I'll create the parity job PR today. Can we aim to get the read-adapter into canary within 4 hours?
jordan: I can cut the PR now, ETA 2h for tests + canary config.
alex: One more ask: can the console dashboard render both 'legacy_count' and 'denorm_count' side-by-side for the canary orgs? Helpful for product & billing to eyeball differences. Small UX change but high value.
mira: I'll add a toggle in the dashboard settings for that. UX team fine with temporary toggle.

deploy-bot: rollout update: console-read-adapter v0.1 deployed to canary group (5%) at 2026-03-21T02:08Z — status: success

sam: Thanks. After canary we should run the hourly parity job and review results in 2 runs before expanding to 25%.
pat: I'll prep backfill runbook in case. Include queries to compute per-tenant diffs, safe backfill windows, and index throttle knobs.
aj: (small note) make sure the billing team signs off on the definition of active_tokens. last time that caught us in contracts.
sam: Noted — @billing-lead I'll ping once we have the snapshot.

mira: OK. I'll keep an eye on the canary dashboards and post a short summary in 3h. :thumbsup:
sam: Thanks everyone. We'll sync if parity > 2% after 2 runs.
